title: Systematic Parameter Setting for Injection Molding

headline.value: SYSTEMATIC PARAMETER SETTING FOR INJECTION MOULDING
headline.note: Title from content/modules.json, with Moulding spelling to match the site's headings.

promise.value: Introduce a consistent framework for parameter-setting decisions.

seriesOutcome.value: Promote a logical, shared approach to process-setting discussions.

items.title: Settings are copied from the last job
items.description: A previous setup is reused on a different tool or material without checking whether it still applies.

items.title: No agreed order for setting a process
items.description: Two engineers reach a workable process by different routes, so neither can explain the other's.

items.title: Changes are made without a stated reason
items.description: A parameter moves to fix one symptom and creates another nobody connects to it.

items.title: Discussions rely on opinion
items.description: Production and engineering disagree about a setting with no shared framework to resolve it.

items.title: Records do not explain the decision
items.description: The sheet shows the final numbers but not why they are those numbers.

items.title: Setup depends on who is on shift
items.description: The same job runs differently depending on which engineer set the machine.

items.title: Consistent setups across shifts
items.description: One method produces the same process whoever is running it.

items.title: Faster, more confident decision-making
items.description: A defined order removes the guesswork from where to start.

items.title: Fewer 'fix one, break another' changes
items.description: Decisions are made in sequence, so the effect of each is visible.

items.title: Shared language between teams
items.description: Production, engineering and quality discuss settings using the same terms.

items.title: Setups that can be repeated and audited
items.description: The record explains the reasoning, not only the final figures.

rows.before: Copies settings from the previous job
rows.after: Establishes settings in a defined order, starting from what the material requires

rows.before: Adjusts a parameter to quiet a symptom
rows.after: States the reason for each change and checks its effect before moving on

rows.before: Explains a setting from memory or experience
rows.after: Explains a setting from the method and the recorded evidence

whyMatters.heading: Why Order Matters More Than Any Number
whyMatters.statement: A SETTING IS A DECISION, NOT A NUMBER TO COPY. When the order of decisions is shared, a process can be explained, repeated and improved by anyone on the team. This module builds that order, so the four-day programme can develop it further.

items.title: Explain why a setting is a decision rather than a value
items.description: State what a chosen parameter is intended to achieve.

items.title: Apply a defined order when setting up a process
items.description: Establish parameters in sequence rather than adjusting at random.

items.title: Justify a parameter change with evidence
items.description: Support each move with an observation rather than an opinion.

items.title: Record settings so another engineer can repeat them
items.description: Capture the reasoning alongside the numbers.

items.title: Discuss a setting using shared terminology
items.description: Take part in a production-versus-engineering discussion with a common framework.

days.label: DAY 1
topics: Machine settings are inputs, not proof - revisiting what a parameter actually does
The four plastic conditions as the frame for every setting decision
A defined order for setting up a process, and why the order is not arbitrary
Why there are no universal setpoints: method over recipes

days.label: DAY 2
topics: Connecting each setting to an observable effect before moving to the next
Justifying a change: what evidence supports a parameter move
Recording a setup so it can be repeated by another engineer
Agreeing terminology for setting discussions across production, engineering and quality

audience.heading: Who Should Attend
items: Process engineers who set and adjust injection moulding parameters
Setup technicians responsible for repeatable changeovers
Production supervisors who approve a running process
Quality engineers involved in setting-related discussions

philosophy.heading: Philosophy
lines: Observe the evidence. Understand the material. Connect the cause-and-effect.

managementTakeaway.value: Consistency at the machine is a decision-making problem before it is a technical one. Two days here gives the team one order for setting a process, so the same job runs the same way on every shift.

safetyNotice.value: Equipment operation, process changes and mould service are restricted to qualified, authorised personnel.
